must_fix.title: Nested Dialogs mounted open together: outer dialog takes focus and Escape, contradicting README's innermost-dialog guarantee
must_fix.evidence: Dialog.tsx pushes onto `openDialogs` in useEffect; child effects run before parent effects, so the outer dialog ends up last ("top") and its effect refocuses itself because the inner portal is outside it. Probe: render(<Dialog open onOpenChange={onA} title="A"><button>a</button><Dialog open onOpenChange={onB} title="B"><button>b</button></Dialog></Dialog>); userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}') -> output 'focused: a' and 'A 1 B 0' (outer closed, inner untouched). README: 'Nested dialogs: only the innermost open dialog responds to Escape, Tab and focus changes.' No test covers this case.

nits: Test describe titles carry unexplained spec codes like (T1), (D3), (C9 and C10), (G1) that refer to a document not in the repo

Dialog: description={false} counts as present, so it renders an empty

and sets aria-describedby
Dialog backdrop can't take props, so it can only be styled via [data-dialog-backdrop]
Combobox 'No results' role=status is inserted together with its text, so some screen readers may not announce it
Combobox optionId gives the same id to values "1" and 1 when they are mixed
TabList runs its key handling even when the user's onKeyDown calls preventDefault

report:
I'd merge this after one fix: when two nested dialogs mount already open, the outer dialog gets focus and handles Escape. Everything else held up. **Checks:** `pnpm test` passes (5 files, 118 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) runs clean. The repo has no lint or format tooling. **Behaviour I checked in a temporary probe test (now deleted; `git status` is back to how I found it):** - **Tabs:** arrow keys wrap and skip disabled tabs, Home and End jump to the ends, only one tab is in the tab order, and with no `defaultValue` the first enabled tab is selected. - **Dialog:** in StrictMode, focus moves into the dialog and returns to the opener on Escape. A nested dialog opened later correctly takes Escape for itself and returns focus to the button that opened it. - **Combobox:** inside a Dialog, Escape first closes the list without closing the dialog, and a second Escape closes the dialog. Typing then ArrowDown and Enter selects the option. ArrowUp on a closed list opens it and activates the last enabled option. **Must fix: nested dialogs that mount already open.** `Dialog.tsx` adds each dialog to its `openDialogs` stack inside a `useEffect`. React runs a child's effects before its parent's, so when both mount open the outer dialog ends up on top of the stack. Its effect also pulls focus back to itself, because the inner dialog is in a separate portal and not inside the outer dialog's DOM. That contradicts the README line "only the innermost open dialog responds to Escape, Tab and focus changes". ```tsx render( ); await userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}"); ``` Output: ``` focused: a A 1 B 0 ``` Focus lands in the outer dialog, and Escape closes the outer dialog instead of the inner one. No test covers this case. The fix is to order the stack by nesting, for example with a context or a layout effect that registers the parent first, and to add a test. **Nits:** - Test `describe` titles carry spec codes such as "(T1)", "(D3)", "(C9 and C10)" and "(G1)" that refer to a document that isn't in the repo. - Dialog: `description={false}` counts as present, so it renders an empty `

` and sets `aria-describedby`. - Dialog: the backdrop can't take props, so it can only be styled through `[data-dialog-backdrop]`. - Combobox: the "No results" `role="status"` element is inserted together with its text, so some screen readers may not announce it. - Combobox: with values like `"1"` and `1` mixed, `optionId` produces the same id for both. - TabList: if the user's `onKeyDown` calls `preventDefault()`, the built-in key handling still runs. ```json {"mergeable": false, "must_fix": [{"title": "Nested Dialogs mounted open together: outer dialog takes focus and Escape, contradicting README's innermost-dialog guarantee", "kind": "bug", "evidence": "Dialog.tsx pushes onto `openDialogs` in useEffect; child effects run before parent effects, so the outer dialog ends up last (\"top\") and its effect refocuses itself because the inner portal is outside it.
